A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaVCa study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original NSD analyses, including voxel-caption prediction, comparisons with BrainSCUBA, ablations, and lexical and semantic diversity results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds BOLD5000 experiments, component controls, sensitivity tests, and cross-subject semantic analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed default pipeline retains ridge encoding, optimal-image selection, MiniCPM-V captioning, LLM keyword extraction and filtering, and MeaCap/CBART sentence composition. V2 provides more explicit specifications and evaluates alternative components and ablated variants, without establishing a revision to the default method.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates neural responses only on NSD. V2 adds BOLD5000 with four additional participants and different acquisition conditions and stimulus sets (Appendix A.5). This materially broadens empirical coverage, although BOLD5000 caption-prediction accuracy is evaluated only on held-out COCO-captioned stimuli.

E2.justification: V2 adds a one-keyword/no-Composer comparator to Table 1 and the top-N voxel comparisons; this differs from v1's one-keyword ablation retaining the Composer. It also adds a raw-beta/no-encoding baseline, alternative encoder comparisons, and evaluated SigLIP2, FG-CLIP, CLIP-Text, and BLIP configurations (Tables A3–A5). BrainSCUBA and Concat remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce matched training/validation allocations for encoder comparisons, alternative architectures and evaluation embeddings, training-sample and category-count sweeps, and noun clustering with k = 6. BOLD5000 adds its own preprocessing, 90/10 split, COCO-only test evaluation, and top-100/500/1000 voxel selections. These substantially extend evaluation design; the original NSD headline protocol remains.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's image-count, keyword-count, extractor, temperature, and ROI-shuffling analyses, v2 tests encoder necessity, encoder training and architecture, VLM/MLLM choices, prompting, Composer removal, and evaluator sensitivity. It also adds data-size sensitivity, cross-subject caption similarity, multi-concept cluster counts, and shared semantic-cluster analyses (Appendices A.3–A.5; Figures A11–A13; Table A12).

E5.justification: V1 constructs null correlations from independent Gaussian vectors. V2 instead specifies 1,000 activity-vector permutations per voxel, pooling null correlations across voxels, and explicitly names Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction (A.2.2). This refines the existing significance framework; SD/SE and paired-test reporting remain, without evidence of increased experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Original headline NSD scores and matched diversity/shuffling tables are retained. V2 adds substantial results: for example, subj01 raw-beta versus full-pipeline accuracy is 0.201 versus 0.246 (Table A4), and BOLD5000 top-100 accuracies are 0.2655, 0.1927, 0.1525, and 0.2117 (Table A7). Additional ablation, sensitivity, and cross-subject findings expand the evidence rather than demonstrate version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2.1 adds an explicit candidate-token scoring definition combining weighted log-likelihood, mean optimal-caption similarity, and voxel similarity (Equation A1), where v1 described the guidance verbally. This is a limited addition of mathematical specification, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of accurate, concise, diverse voxel captions remain. V2 additionally claims an interpretability advantage from decomposing captioning into interpretable stages in its first contribution, and its conclusion more explicitly states that the richer ROI representations challenge conventional assumptions about functional specialization.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning encoder-based noise suppression, the value of sentence context, robustness across model and prompt choices, and reproducibility of semantic organization across subjects and datasets. It attributes lower BOLD5000 accuracy to dataset quality rather than NSD overfitting. The existing limitations concerning local face features and multimodal applicability are retained in Appendix A.6.

D1.justification: V2 adds Composer scoring weights, feature normalization, expanded checkpoint information, encoder-training hyperparameters, and hardware, memory, and timing estimates, including approximately 83 hours for 20,000 voxels (A.2–A.3). It explicitly reports public source-code and script availability. These substantially improve documentation, although v1's specific TextGraphParser extraction settings are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds explicit positioning against brain decoding, including Tang et al. and Chen et al., and references supporting BOLD5000, additional backbones, prompting, and sentence embeddings. Several earlier citations are removed. The central relationship to BrainSCUBA and SASC and the full related-work appendix remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction, related work, and implementation explanation; reorganizes the prediction and ROI-analysis narratives; and restructures the appendix into more detailed subsections. Limitations and impact discussion move to the appendix, while ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements are added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figures 1 and 3 are revised, Table 1 is split into sentence/image panels with configuration columns, and Figure 5 replaces the OFA-only summary with four-ROI noun/verb displays. Numerous new tables, sensitivity plots, heatmaps, and cluster visualizations are added, while many original appendix figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's limited validation through component controls, robustness tests, BOLD5000 evaluation, and cross-subject semantic analyses. Together with expanded implementation, resource, and code-access documentation, these additions improve confidence in the method and its reproducibility without relying on higher original headline scores. The gains outweigh remaining weaknesses, including COCO-only BOLD5000 evaluation and new reporting inconsistencies such as Table A2's learning-rate decay factor disagreeing with its formula.
